problem: Existing navigation agents use a fixed forward-looking camera, so they perceive redundant information and explore slowly; few works control the camera actively, and naive camera actions do not help because they are hard to coordinate with navigation actions.
motivation: Humans turn their heads while walking to see more of the environment. Multi-object navigation needs efficient exploration with camera sensors only. Learning a camera policy is hard because of complex RGB-D inputs and because camera and navigation actions are executed simultaneously.
key_idea: Learn an exploration-oriented (EXPO) camera policy with RL that takes a top-down occupancy map, a rule-based heuristic direction and the upcoming navigation action as input, and is rewarded for heuristic-following and explored-area gain.
insight: Naive or rule-based camera actions give little gain or hurt (Table 1, Table 3), while the learned policy trained with heuristic guidance and area reward improves more. Ablations show every input and reward matters, with the heuristic reward most (SPL 57.9 to 53.8 without it). For end-to-end agents, a joint navigation-camera policy is necessary because separate policies drop below the baseline (Table C), since the navigation policy cannot control what it sees.
method: Mapper: converts RGB-D into a local occupancy map (unexplored/free/occupied) and registers it into a global map; uses ground-truth occupancy anticipation.

Heuristic module: samples K=8 points at radius r=2.4 m around the agent, runs A* on the global map (free and unexplored are navigable), and marks points in unexplored area with geodesic distance below γ=2.88 as explorable; picks the one closest to the current camera direction as heuristic direction, else 0.
Policy network: CNN map encoder (512-d), embeddings for heuristic direction and navigation action (32-d), a GRU, and an actor-critic head that outputs TURN-CAMERA-LEFT/RIGHT/KEEP.
Reward: r = α·r_heuristic (reduction of angle to heuristic direction) + β·r_area (explored-area gain) − r_turn-penalty (camera motor actuation), with α=10, β=1; trained with PPO.
Coordination with SLAM-based navigation: the camera policy is conditioned on the navigation action output by the navigation policy, and the planner replans with the map built from the camera output.

Coordination with end-to-end navigation: a single joint recurrent policy takes map, heuristic direction and RGB-D inputs and predicts navigation and camera actions, with summed exploration and navigation rewards.
Action execution: camera and navigation turn angles are equal (30°), so the camera motor is only actuated when the camera must turn differently from the platform.

setting.backbone: EXPO camera policy (CNN + GRU actor-critic, trained with PPO) plugged into OccAnt, Mapping+FBE, MultiON and DD-PPO
setting.training_data: Matterport3D MultiON dataset, 61 training scenes; 2M frames for SLAM-based and 30M frames for end-to-end baselines; Gibson used only for zero-shot transfer testing
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with active camera plus pose; progressively built top-down occupancy map
setting.action_space: discrete: FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN 30°, FOUND (automatic), plus camera actions TURN-CAMERA-LEFT/RIGHT/KEEP
setting.privileged: ground-truth occupancy anticipation map within field of view, perfect camera pose, oracle FOUND action; noisy predicted mapper only in one analysis

numbers.extra: 3-ON, 500 step budget, GT occupancy mapper, oracle FOUND
numbers.evidence: Table 1, Matterport3D, OccAnt + Our Camera Policy

numbers.eval_set_note: 861 self-generated multi-object episodes in 14 Gibson test scenes
numbers.backbone: OccAnt + EXPO camera policy trained on Matterport3D
numbers.evidence: Table 1, Gibson, OccAnt + Our Camera Policy

numbers.backbone: MultiON + EXPO joint policy trained on Matterport3D

numbers_note: Custom multi-object navigation benchmark (MultiON-style, cylinder goals, not among canonical names); test split of MultiON Matterport3D dataset (18 scenes). Also reports Mapping+FBE and DD-PPO on Gibson, and 1-ON/2-ON results in the supplement.
results: The EXPO camera policy consistently improves four baselines on Matterport3D and Gibson (transfer). For example OccAnt SPL rises from 53.0 to 57.9 and Success from 72.0 to 75.6; MultiON Success rises from 44.1 to 51.1. Naive camera actions give no gain or hurt, and a four-fixed-camera agent beats it on SLAM-based agents (SPL 68.3) but not on end-to-end MultiON.
limitations: Relies on ground-truth occupancy anticipation, perfect pose and oracle FOUND; with a predicted noisy map, performance is much lower (SPL 18.1).
Evaluated only in simulation on synthetic cylinder goals; no real-robot test and no actuation noise.
Fails when it picks the wrong direction to explore; no semantic priors on object location; SLAM-based multi-fixed cameras outperform it.
compares_to: Swing and heuristic rule-based camera actions
